jobs.title: THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE · The stone head walks
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; CHLOE — aged 18, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders, oversized dark cardigan, a Discman on her belt with headphones around her neck, a folded-back paperback, reads while talking. Title of the strip: BACKUP. The strip: The night before Halloween: the moss-grown face by the bait shack's wall is gone from the grass, and its shape is on the seawall, and then on the school's steps, and then back in the grass with a dead leaf on its brow. Nobody sees it move. The strip draws where it was, three times. Panel 1: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, two teenagers looking at a face-shaped hollow in grass beside a shingle wall at night (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE). Chloe says "It was here. It's always here.". Panel 2: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a moss-grown carved stone head sitting on a seawall at night facing the bay with a gull perched on it. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a moss-grown carved stone head sitting on a school's front steps at night. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a moss-grown carved stone head back in grass by a wall with a dead leaf on its brow and a teenage girl's hand reaching for the leaf (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Wood says "Don't.". Chloe says "It's a leaf.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
